claim: Sperm production is a continuous process. A full cycle of spermatogenesis takes roughly two to two-and-a-half months, so sperm are not simply stored up indefinitely from the moment ejaculation stops.
review_note: Title to be confirmed by the medical reviewer against the PubMed record.

claim: Longer ejaculatory abstinence tends to increase semen volume and the total number of sperm available in an ejaculate.
source_title: Revisiting the relationship between the ejaculatory abstinence period and semen characteristics (Int J Fertil Steril, 2018)

claim: Longer abstinence does not mean every measure of sperm quality keeps improving. Longer intervals have been associated with lower progressive motility and higher sperm DNA fragmentation, while shorter intervals can be preferable for those measures.
source_title: PubMed 38828413 - ejaculatory abstinence, motility and sperm DNA fragmentation (2024)
review_note: Supported also by PubMed 41809803 (2026) and 29143943 (2018). Titles to be confirmed by the medical reviewer.

claim: The WHO laboratory manual asks for 2 to 7 days of ejaculatory abstinence before a semen sample. That is a laboratory standardisation window so results can be compared, not a recommendation that anyone should retain semen for health.
source_title: WHO laboratory manual for the examination and processing of human semen, 6th edition (2021)

claim: An individual's sperm concentration, count, motility and morphology can only be measured by a laboratory semen analysis. No app timer can estimate them.
source_title: WHO laboratory manual for the examination and processing of human semen, 6th edition (2021)

claim: Male ageing is associated with declines in semen volume, motility, progressive motility, normal morphology and DNA integrity. A large meta-analysis did not find a consistent decline in sperm concentration with age, so there is no universal fixed percentage decline per year.
source_title: Consistent age-dependent declines in human semen quality: a systematic review and meta-analysis (Ageing Research Reviews, 2015)

claim: Individual studies have estimated different age effects on semen quality, including some that reported declines in concentration. Results differ enough that a single regression formula should not be applied to every man.
source_title: PubMed 16225533 - age and semen parameters, single-population study
review_note: Title and year to be confirmed by the medical reviewer.

claim: There is no strong evidence that abstaining from ejaculation raises testosterone in a lasting way. One small study reported a short-term fluctuation around day seven of abstinence that then returned toward baseline; it has not been replicated at scale.
source_title: A research on the relationship between ejaculation and serum testosterone level in men (J Zhejiang Univ Sci, 2003)
review_note: n=28. Frequently over-cited online; present only as limited evidence.

claim: Claims that semen retention produces supernatural energy, magnetism or special powers come from tradition and personal testimony, not from controlled scientific evidence.
review_note: Displayed with the white 'tradition' label only.

claim: Urges rise, peak and pass on their own within minutes. Practising 'urge surfing', noticing the urge without acting, has been shown to reduce acting on cravings.
source_title: Surfing the urge: brief mindfulness-based intervention for college student smokers (Psychology of Addictive Behaviors, 2009)
review_note: Studied in smoking; generalisation to sexual urges is reasonable but indirect.

claim: Poor or short sleep is associated with weaker self-control and more impulsive decisions the following day.
source_title: Interactions between sleep habits and self-control (Frontiers in Human Neuroscience, 2015)

claim: Regular physical exercise is associated with better mood and gains in self-regulation that carry over into other areas of life.
source_title: Longitudinal gains in self-regulation from regular physical exercise (British Journal of Health Psychology, 2006)

claim: Even mild dehydration can worsen mood, concentration and the feeling of effort in healthy adults.
source_title: Mild dehydration impairs cognitive performance and mood of men (British Journal of Nutrition, 2011)

claim: New habits take weeks to months to become automatic, and the time varies widely between people. Missing a single day does not undo the habit.
source_title: How are habits formed: modelling habit formation in the real world (European Journal of Social Psychology, 2010)
review_note: Median 66 days; range 18 to 254 days. Never show the number as a promise.

claim: Deciding in advance exactly what you will do when a trigger appears ('If it is 11 PM and I am scrolling, then I put the phone in the kitchen') reliably improves follow-through on goals.
source_title: Implementation intentions and goal achievement: a meta-analysis of effects and processes (Advances in Experimental Social Psychology, 2006)

claim: Sperm DNA fragmentation tends to increase with age. This is one of the reproductive parameters most consistently linked to ageing.
source_title: Consistent age-dependent declines in human semen quality: a systematic review and meta-analysis (Ageing Research Reviews, 2015)

claim: In some fertility-treatment settings, shorter abstinence intervals have been associated with better outcomes for motility and DNA integrity. Anyone planning a pregnancy should follow their clinician's advice rather than an app.
source_title: PubMed 41809803 - abstinence interval and fertility outcomes (2026)
review_note: Title to be confirmed by the medical reviewer.
